literal: Qian drew the bow and shot them, one arrow killing two or three men; those shaking the spear scattered souls and fled; leisurely he had someone fetch the spear and left.
idiomatic: Qian turned, loosed his bow, and dropped two or three men per shaft; those tugging at the spear fled in terror; then he calmly sent men to retrieve the weapon and rode away.

literal: Each time he followed on campaign and as wing general, he constantly first climbed and broke formations, courage foremost of the age; enemies regardless of numbers dared not withstand those before him.
idiomatic: On every campaign, as a flank commander, he was always first over the wall; none in his day matched his courage, and no enemy, few or many, stood before him.

literal: When he died.
idiomatic: When he died,

literal: The whole state mourned and wept for him, flowing tears; Daowu many times pursuing memory hurt and grieved.
idiomatic: the whole realm mourned and wept; Emperor Daowu grieved for him again and again.

literal: Posthumously Prince of Chenliu Huan, enshrined in the ancestral temple, his son Yue enfeoffed Prince of Zhuti.
idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Prince Huan of Chenliu, enshrined in the ancestral temple; his son Yue was enfeoffed Prince of Zhuti.

literal: Yue outwardly harmonious inwardly fierce.
idiomatic: Yue was outwardly mild and inwardly savage.

literal: Daowu because the Huan prince died for the state specially added intimate favor, made Left General, inherited the fief, later became Imperial Clan Mentor.
idiomatic: Because Prince Huan had died for the state, Daowu favored Yue especially, made him Left General, let him inherit the fief, and later named him Imperial Clan Mentor.

literal: Yue relied on favor and was arrogant; each time said to intimates Wang Luosheng and company: "Once the imperial carriage halts, I only avoid the Duke of Wei."
idiomatic: Arrogant with favor, Yue told intimates such as Wang Luosheng: "When the emperor dies I need only step aside for the Prince of Wei."

literal: Aside from this, who is before me!"
idiomatic: Who else would stand before me?"

literal: Prince of Wei Yi had beautiful beard, valued inside and out, therefore Yue spoke thus.
idiomatic: The Prince of Wei Yi wore a splendid beard and was respected throughout the court, which is why Yue spoke so.

literal: At first when Yao Xing ransomed Di Bozhi, Yue escorted him; the route passed Yanmen.
idiomatic: When Yao Xing ransomed Di Bozhi, Yue escorted him along the road through Yanmen.

literal: Yue thereby in secret enticed treacherous notables to win their favor.
idiomatic: On the way Yue secretly courted local strongmen to win their support.

literal: Later encountering reproof he fled, threw himself into Yanmen, scheming to gather heroes intending treason, captured by locals and sent.
idiomatic: Later, censured, he fled to Yanmen, plotted to rally bold men for rebellion, and was seized by locals and sent to court.

literal: The emperor forgave without punishing.
idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him.

literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, brought Yue in to attend, still harboring wicked plans, told the emperor: "Capital strangers cannot be trusted for faithful guarding—should execute those not of our kind."
idiomatic: When Mingyuan ascended, Yue attended court still plotting. He told the emperor: "The strangers in the capital cannot be trusted; execute those who are not of us."

literal: Also said: "Yanmen people are mostly deceitful—all can be executed."
idiomatic: He also said: "The people of Yanmen are mostly deceitful and should all be killed."

literal: Wishing to clear his private resentment; the emperor did not follow.
idiomatic: He meant to settle private scores; the emperor refused.

literal: Yue inwardly suspicious and afraid, carried a blade entering attendance, plotting great treason.
idiomatic: Fearful and suspicious, Yue entered attendance with a blade hidden, intending treason.

literal: Shusun Jun suspected him.
idiomatic: Shusun Jun grew suspicious.

literal: Secretly seeing a blade in his bosom, seized and granted death.
idiomatic: Finding a blade in his bosom, Jun seized him and he was put to death.

literal: Son Jian inherited, demoted noble rank to duke, post General Who Pacifies the North, great general of Huaihuang Garrison.
idiomatic: His son Jian inherited, was demoted to duke, and became General Who Pacifies the North and commander of Huaihuang Garrison.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Jian's son Chen, posts Inspector of Heng and Yi.
idiomatic: Jian's son Chen served as Inspector of Heng and Yi.

literal: Chen's son Yi, Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy.
idiomatic: Chen's son Yi became Left Deputy of the Secretariat.

literal: Yi's son Hui.
idiomatic: Yi's son was Hui.

literal: Hui styled Shuping, beard and brows like painting, bearing admirable.
idiomatic: Hui, styled Shuping, had painted brows and an admirable bearing.

literal: Fond of ranging through books and records, in youth gained fine name in the capital.
idiomatic: He loved books and in youth won a fine name in the capital.

literal: Zhou Wendi honored him, ordered him to roam and dwell with the princes, each time shared inkstone and mat, affection extremely thick.
idiomatic: Zhou Wendi honored him, had him keep company with the princes, shared desk and mat with them, and grew deeply fond of him.

literal: Again promoted Junior Grand Master of Martial Dukes.
idiomatic: He was again promoted Junior Grand Master of Martial Dukes.

literal: At that time the Türks repeatedly were border troubles; the court was about to form marriage alliance, ordered Hui to buy brocades one hundred thousand, envoys to the Türks.
idiomatic: The Türks raided repeatedly; as the court prepared a marriage alliance, Hui was sent with a hundred thousand worth of brocade.

literal: Hui persuaded with profit and harm; the khan greatly pleased, sent his famous king following with tribute goods.
idiomatic: Hui argued profit and peril; the khan was delighted and sent a royal prince with tribute.

literal: Soon appointed Colonel Peer of Three Ranks.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Colonel of the Third Rank.

literal: When Zhou Wudi married the Türkish queen, ordered Hui to convey rites.
idiomatic: When Zhou Wudi married a Türkish princess, Hui was sent to convey the rites.

literal: Granted Opening the Office, transferred Grand Master of the Bureau of Justice.
idiomatic: He was granted Opening the Office and made Grand Master of the Bureau of Justice.

literal: When pacifying Guandong, made Hui settle Hebei, enfeoffed Viscount of Yining.
idiomatic: When Guandong was pacified, Hui was sent to settle Hebei and enfeoffed Viscount of Yining.

literal: When Emperor Wendi of Sui oversaw all affairs, added Upper Opening the Office, advanced noble rank to duke.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui held the reins of power, Hui was made Upper Opener of the Office and raised to duke.

literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, appointed Minister of Justice, concurrently overseeing Grand Master of Equipage.
idiomatic: At the start of Kaihuang he became Minister of Justice and also oversaw the Grand Master of Equipage.

literal: Received edict to channel Duyang water to irrigate Sanzhi Plain, irrigating several thousand qing of salty land; people relied on the benefit.
idiomatic: By edict he diverted the Duyang River to irrigate Sanzhi Plain, reclaiming thousands of qing of salty soil; the people prospered.

literal: Again transferred Minister of War, supervised the canal transport service.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of War and supervised the canal works.

literal: Before long, because of affairs dismissed.
idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed for an offense.

literal: Shortly after, appointed Inspector of Weizhou, had considerable benevolent government.
idiomatic: Soon after he was made Inspector of Weizhou and governed with notable kindness.

literal: Later because of illness left office, died in the capital.
idiomatic: Later he resigned for illness and died in the capital.

literal: The emperor mourned long, ordered Minister of Ceremonies oversee funeral, posthumous title Primal.
idiomatic: The emperor mourned at length, ordered the Minister of Ceremonies to oversee the funeral, and gave the posthumous title Primal.

literal: Son Su inherited, post Vice Director of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: His son Su inherited and became Vice Director of Splendid Happiness.

literal: Su's younger brother Ren, disposition and nature bright and keen, post Assistant of Rinan Commandery.
idiomatic: Su's younger brother Ren was clever and sharp and became Assistant Administrator of Rinan.

literal: Jian's younger brother's eldest son Zuo, styled Longshou.
idiomatic: Jian's younger brother's eldest son Zuo, styled Longshou.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu reviewed martial arts; each year's end edict ordered teaching and practicing military exercise.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu held martial reviews; at each year's end an edict ordered drill and practice.

literal: At first Jian because his son's crime lost the noble rank; Zuo wished to seek the original enfeoffment.
idiomatic: Jian had lost his noble rank because of his son's crime; Zuo sought to recover the original fief.

literal: The relevant office memorialized permitting Zuo to inherit the duke; the prince's rank was not light—together sought further discussion; edict followed.
idiomatic: The authorities memorialized that Zuo might inherit as duke, but a princely title was weighty; they asked for further deliberation, and the edict agreed.

literal: Died as Inspector of Hezhou.
idiomatic: He died as Inspector of Hezhou.

literal: At the time of Emperor Jiemin, posthumously Attendant-in-Ordinary, Deputy Minister of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Jiemin he was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Deputy Minister of the Secretariat.

literal: Qian's elder brother Yan, nature stern and grave, few words.
idiomatic: Qian's elder brother Yan was stern, grave, and sparing of speech.

literal: Daowu constantly respected him, in elegance had stratagems.
idiomatic: Daowu respected him and valued his counsel.

literal: Following the pacification of Zhongshan, for merit granted noble rank Marquis of Pucheng.
idiomatic: After the pacification of Zhongshan he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pucheng for merit.

literal: Especially seen with thick favor, given drum wind feathered instruments, rites equal to highest inspectors.
idiomatic: He received exceptional favor: drums, winds, and feathered banners, with rites equal to a frontier inspector.

literal: Holding government by prestige and trust famed, in office seven years, then Yuan Yigan replaced Yan as prefecture.
idiomatic: He governed seven years on prestige and trust, then Yuan Yigan replaced him as prefect.

literal: At that time Yigan's son Wanyan gained favor with Daowu; Yigan relied on his son, slighted Yan without informing his situation, light cavalry suddenly arrived, pushed Yan off the couch and occupied his seat.
idiomatic: Yigan's son Wanyan was then in favor. Relying on this, Yigan rode in without warning, shoved Yan from his seat, and took his place.

literal: Yan did not know he was replaced, thought he was seized for crime.
idiomatic: Yan, not knowing he had been replaced, thought he was being arrested for a crime.

literal: Once he knew, ashamed of the insult, said to Yigan: "My turn fully filled being replaced—that is constant."
idiomatic: When he understood, ashamed of the insult, he told Yigan: "Serving out my term and being replaced—that is ordinary."

literal: You insulted me without propriety—how can that be tolerated!"
idiomatic: But you dishonored me without courtesy—that cannot be borne!"

literal: Thereupon grappled and killed him.
idiomatic: He grappled with Yigan and killed him.

literal: Memorializing the full situation, Daowu admired him.
idiomatic: He reported the matter fully; Daowu admired his spirit.

literal: Wanyan repeatedly sued and requested; then edict Yan pay ransom.
idiomatic: Wanyan sued repeatedly; an edict ordered Yan to pay blood-money.

literal: Yan then himself requested punishment; Daowu pardoned him, again exempted the ransom.
idiomatic: Yan then asked to be punished; Daowu pardoned him and waived the ransom.

literal: Died of illness.
idiomatic: He died of illness.

literal: Prince of Piling Shun was Diggan's son.
idiomatic: Prince of Piling Shun was Diggan's son.

literal: Nature coarse and fierce.
idiomatic: He was coarse and fierce by nature.

literal: At the beginning of the state's founding, granted noble rank Duke of Nan'an.
idiomatic: At the founding of the state he was enfeoffed Duke of Nan'an.

literal: When Daowu attacked Zhongshan, left Shun guarding the capital.
idiomatic: When Daowu attacked Zhongshan he left Shun to guard the capital.

literal: After the defeat at Baisi, soldiers returned saying the great army scattered in flight, not knowing where the emperor was.
idiomatic: After the defeat at Baisi, fugitive soldiers said the main force had scattered and the emperor's whereabouts were unknown.

literal: Hearing this, Shun wished to set himself up; Namodi remonstrated, then stopped.
idiomatic: Hearing this, Shun meant to declare himself ruler; Namodi dissuaded him and he stopped.

literal: At that time Helijuan and others gathered crowds making chaos at Yin Studio; Shun attacked but did not overcome.
idiomatic: Helijuan and others were then raising trouble at Yin Studio; Shun attacked but could not defeat them.

literal: Then from the remaining officials himself from Baideng south entered Fanzhi old city, blocking the levee waters as defense, to settle people's hearts.
idiomatic: He withdrew with the officials left in the capital from Baideng south to the old city of Fanzhi, dammed the waters as a defense, and steadied men's hearts.

literal: Daowu praised this, advanced enfeoffment to prince, post Colonel of the Capital District.
idiomatic: Daowu praised him, raised him to prince, and made him Colonel of the Capital District.

literal: Daowu loved Yellow Emperor and Laozi, repeatedly summoned princes and court ministers personally to lecture—those seated none not reverent, only Shun alone sat sleeping, not looking and spat.
idiomatic: Daowu loved the Yellow Emperor and Laozi and often lectured princes and ministers himself. All sat in reverence; only Shun dozed, looked away, and spat.

literal: The emperor in anger deposed him.
idiomatic: The emperor in anger deposed him.

literal: The prince died at home.
idiomatic: The prince died at home.

literal: Duke of Liaoxi Yilie was Lizhen's son.
idiomatic: Duke of Liaoxi Yilie was Lizhen's son.

literal: First died at Murong Chui's place.
idiomatic: He had earlier died in Murong Chui's domain.

literal: Daowu campaigning Zhongshan, abandoned wife and children welcoming at Jingxing.
idiomatic: When Daowu campaigned against Zhongshan, he abandoned wife and children to welcome the emperor at Jingxing.

literal: When pacifying the Central Plains, had battle merits, granted noble rank Duke of Liaoxi, made Administrator of Guangping.
idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified he won battle honors, was enfeoffed Duke of Liaoxi, and made Administrator of Guangping.

literal: At that time He Ba was Xingtai of Ye; Yilie by nature fierce and unyielding, himself as imperial kin ashamed to be under Ba, thereupon secretly formed a party, about to attack Ye.
idiomatic: He Ba was then Xingtai of Ye. Proud as imperial kin, Yilie resented serving under him, secretly gathered a faction, and plotted to seize Ye.

literal: Discovered, granted death.
idiomatic: The plot was discovered and he was sentenced to death.

literal: Son Bagan, broadly knew past and present.
idiomatic: His son Bagan was broadly learned in past and present.

literal: Though his father had crime, Daowu because Bagan was imperial kin entrusted him heart and belly.
idiomatic: Though his father had sinned, Daowu trusted Bagan as kin and kept him close.

literal: Had stratagems, repeatedly showed loyalty and diligence.
idiomatic: He was resourceful and repeatedly proved loyal and diligent.

literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, made Administrator of Bohai; officials and people delighted.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan ascended he made Bagan Administrator of Bohai, to the joy of officials and people.

literal: Granted noble rank Viscount of Wusui, transferred General Who Pacifies Pingyuan, gained officers' and soldiers' hearts.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Wusui, made General Who Pacifies Pingyuan, and won the hearts of officers and men.

literal: He died, posthumous title Duke Spiritual.
idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Spiritual Duke.

literal: Son Shouluo inherited, advanced noble rank Duke of Wuyi.
idiomatic: His son Shouluo inherited and was raised to Duke of Wuyi.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Son Chinu, General of Wuchuan Garrison.
idiomatic: His son Chinu was general of Wuchuan Garrison.

literal: Chinu's son Hongchao had considerable learning; after the Great Vehicle rebels' chaos, edict Hongchao hold staff concurrently Yellow Gate Attendant, pacify Ji.
idiomatic: Chinu's son Hongchao was learned. After the Great Vehicle rebellion, he was sent with staff and as Yellow Gate Attendant to pacify Ji.

literal: Returning, memorialized that Ji was broad, border several hundred li from the province, backed on sea dangerous and far—should divide and establish a province to suppress the sea bend.
idiomatic: On his return he memorialized that Ji was vast, its coast hundreds of li from the provincial seat and hard to govern—another province should be carved out to control the seaboard.

literal: Court discussion followed; later indeed established Cangzhou.
idiomatic: The court agreed; Cangzhou was later established.

literal: Died as General of the Northern Army, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: He died as General of the Northern Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

literal: Yilie's younger brother Bo, skilled at shooting and charioteering, for merit granted noble rank Duke of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: Yilie's younger brother Bo excelled at archery and chariotry and was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng for merit.

literal: He died, posthumous title Que.
idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Que.

literal: Buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He was buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: Eldest son Su inherited.
idiomatic: His eldest son Su inherited.
